---
name: project_purge_docs
description: "Find and delete obsolete documents generated by an AI assistant (old plans, finished analyses) while protecting real documentation. Asks before deleting"
---

Clean up the noise left by AI-generated documents that are no longer useful (implementation plans already executed, finished analyses, one-off notes), without touching documentation that gives lasting context. Deleting files is hard to undo, so work in phases and never delete before the user confirms.

Scope or extra instructions (optional: a folder, or a hint about what to keep): <the text the user wrote with the skill invocation, if any>

Context (run these commands first and use their output):
- Git state: `git status --short --branch`

Phase 1 - Find candidates (read-only)
- Look at documentation-type files only (`.md`, `.txt`, `.rst`, `.adoc`), skipping `.git`, `node_modules`, vendor and build folders.
- A file is a candidate when there are signs it was generated by an AI assistant (Codex, Claude or another) as working material:
  - It lives in a typical plan or spec location (`docs/superpowers/`, `docs/plans/`, `plans/`, `specs/`, `.claude/plans/`, `.codex/plans/`, `analysis/`, `notes/`), or its name looks like `*_PLAN.md`, `*_ANALYSIS.md`, `*_SUMMARY.md`, `*_REPORT.md`, `IMPLEMENTATION*.md`, `TODO*.md`, `NOTES*.md`.
  - Its content reads as working material: task lists with checkboxes, "Implementation plan", step-by-step prompts to an agent, status or progress reports, "Generated with Codex" or "Generated with Claude" footers.
  - Git history shows it was added in commits made with or by an AI assistant (Co-Authored-By trailers) and not edited by anyone else afterwards.
- Check whether it is still useful: are its tasks done (checkboxes ticked, the code or tests it describes already exist, related branch merged)? Is it referenced from anywhere (README, other docs, code, config; use `git grep` for its path and name)?

Phase 2 - Protect (never propose these for deletion)
- Project documentation that gives lasting context: README, `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, CONTRIBUTING, LICENSE, CHANGELOG.
- Documents describing the app as it is: architecture, design, data model, API documentation, decision records (ADR), runbooks, setup and usage guides, user manuals.
- Datasheets, specifications of external systems, contracts, reference material and anything provided by people (not generated).
- Any file referenced by the README, other kept documents, code, build or config files.
- Any file with commits from human authors only, or that you cannot clearly tell was AI working material.
- When in doubt, keep it. The default is never delete.

Phase 3 - Propose (nothing is deleted yet)
Show a table with every candidate: path, size, what it is in one plain line, evidence it is obsolete (tasks done, implemented in which place, last touched, not referenced), whether it is tracked by git (recoverable) or untracked (NOT recoverable once deleted), and your confidence (high or unsure).
Split it in three groups: "Safe to delete (high confidence)", "Review (unsure)", and a short count of what was protected and why, without listing every protected file.
For "Review" items that still describe how a feature works, mention that their useful content could be moved into the real documentation first. Do not do it unless asked.
Then ask the user which to delete, and wait. Accept answers such as "all the safe ones" or specific numbers.

Phase 4 - Delete (only after confirmation)
- Delete only what the user confirmed, nothing else. Untracked files need an explicit extra confirmation that names them.
- Do not commit and do not stage anything. Deleted tracked files stay recoverable with `git restore <path>`.
- Afterwards report what was deleted, how to recover it, and any broken links left in other documents (list them, do not fix them without asking).

Reply following the global communication rules.
